'Creating a love for learning'
Welcome from our Headteacher
A very warm welcome to Peppard Church of England Primary School. Our vision is to provide every child with the opportunity to flourish academically, socially and spiritually within a caring and supportive Christian community. Guided by the words “Encourage one another and build each other up” (1 Thessalonians 5:11), we nurture children in an environment where they feel safe, valued and confident to grow and achieve their full potential.
At Peppard, our school values of Kindness, Respect and Perseverance, are lived out every day. They guide our teaching, learning and relationships, inspiring children to aim high, make thoughtful choices and contribute positively to our community. Through a broad and engaging curriculum, rich learning experiences and a wide range of extracurricular opportunities, we encourage every child to develop curiosity, resilience and a love of learning.
Our most recent Ofsted inspection recognised the many strengths of our school. Inspectors highlighted the calm, nurturing environment created by staff, where pupils feel safe, valued and part of a close and supportive community. They praised pupils’ exemplary behaviour, enthusiasm for learning and confidence in speaking about their work, reflecting the strong culture and high expectations that run throughout the school.
The report also recognised the strength of our early reading provision and the carefully planned curriculum that helps pupils build knowledge and skills over time. Classrooms are purposeful and engaging, and pupils approach their learning with enthusiasm and pride. Importantly, inspectors noted that pupils themselves describe Peppard as feeling like “a family,” reflecting the strong relationships that underpin our school community.
Our small-school setting allows us to know every child as an individual. This enables us to provide personalised support while creating a strong sense of belonging for pupils and families alike. Our beautiful rural location offers opportunities for outdoor learning and exploration, helping children develop independence, curiosity and a deeper understanding of the world around them.
We believe that education extends beyond the classroom. Pupils benefit from a rich programme of trips, sports, music and leadership opportunities that help build confidence, teamwork and responsibility. These experiences allow children to discover their strengths and develop the character and skills needed for the future.
Our close links with All Saints’ Church enrich the spiritual life of the school, but we warmly welcome families of all faiths and none. What unites us is a shared commitment to a safe, inclusive and joyful community where every child can thrive.
As Headteacher, I am incredibly proud of our pupils, staff and families who together make Peppard such a special place to learn and grow.
I warmly invite you to explore our website and, even better, to visit us in person. You can be assured of a very warm welcome.
Please contact myself or Fiona Hilton to arrange a visit.
We look forward to welcoming you.
Mrs K WakefieldHeadteacher

Reception Information for Parents starting in 2026-2027
Welcome to Peppard Church of England Primary School.
We are delighted to be welcoming you and your child to our school community. Starting school is a significant and exciting milestone, and we are committed to making this transition as smooth, positive and reassuring as possible for both children and their families.
Miss Lawrence and Mrs Wakefield are very much looking forward to meeting you all and welcoming you into your new class. We place great importance on helping children feel safe, secure and happy from the very beginning, so that they can settle quickly and begin to enjoy their learning.
Information will be sent to you through the school office regarding upcoming transition opportunities, including stay-and-play sessions, parent information meetings and Forest School experiences. These are carefully planned to support children in becoming familiar with the school environment, building confidence and forming strong relationships with staff and their peers as early as possible.
Below you will find copies of letters and information that the school office has already sent, or will be sending shortly. These are included here in case you need any additional copies for reference.
We look forward to welcoming you soon and beginning this exciting journey together.
Peppard Church of England Primary School
Church Lane, Peppard, Henley-on-Thames, RG9 5JU
School Office 01491 628354
office@peppardprimary.co.uk

pageCache.text:
Student Login
Clubs and Wrap Around Care
Autumn Term Clubs 2026
We are delighted to share our Autumn Term Clubs Timetable.
Our clubs will run from Monday 7th September until Friday 11th December and offer a wide range of opportunities for children to develop new skills, build confidence, make new friendships and enjoy learning beyond the classroom.
This term sees the return of many of our popular clubs, alongside some exciting new additions. We hope there is something to inspire every child.
Bookings will open at 5.00pm on Thursday 3rd September. Full details about each club, including booking information, can be found below.
We look forward to another exciting term of clubs and seeing as many children as possible enjoying the fantastic opportunities on offer.
Wrap Around Care Club is the ultimate place for children to feel safe, happy, and inspired! Our wrap-around care program is designed to support families by offering reliable, fun, and engaging care before and after school, where every child is warmly welcomed.
At Wrap Around Care Club, children have the opportunity to enjoy healthy snacks, play with their friends, and take part in a variety of exciting activities. Whether it’s exploring creativity through art, learning new recipes in cooking sessions, moving to the rhythm in dance, or staying active with sports and games, there’s something for every interest and personality.
We pride ourselves on creating a friendly and inclusive environment where children can grow, learn, and have fun in equal measure. Our dedicated team is passionate about ensuring every child feels valued, engaged, and inspired throughout their time with us. With Warap Around Care Club, families can have peace of mind knowing their children are in a safe, nurturing space where friendships flourish, curiosity is encouraged, and every day is full of joyful experiences.
Booking your child’s place at Wrap Around Care Club is simple! You can reserve spots in advance online through School Spider, or if plans change, just give us a call on the day – we’ll do our best to accommodate you.
Led by Mrs Wakefield and Mrs Smith, Art & Craft Club provides children with the opportunity to explore their creativity in a fun and inspiring environment. Using a wide range of artistic materials and techniques, children develop new skills, experiment with different media and create high-quality pieces of artwork they can be proud of, all while expressing their own unique ideas and imagination.
Cost: £7.50 per session.
Start the day full of energy with our popular Running Club, led by Mrs Elson. Whether children are developing their running technique, improving their fitness or taking part in fun games and challenges, every session is designed to build confidence, resilience and a love of being active. It's a fantastic way to enjoy the fresh morning air and begin the school day feeling positive and ready to learn.
Cost: £7.50 per session.
Our thriving LAMDA Club, led by Mrs Gridler, helps children grow in confidence while developing their public speaking and performance skills. Through engaging activities, speech work and drama, children learn to communicate clearly, express themselves with confidence and speak effectively in a range of situations, valuable skills that will benefit them throughout their lives. Kate.lamda@outlook.com
Led by Amanda Watkins-Cooke, our thriving Netball Club is perfect for children of all abilities. Through exciting games, skill-building activities and friendly competition, children develop teamwork, coordination and confidence while enjoying one of the country's most popular team sports.
Cost: £7.50 per session.
Our Cookery Club gives children the opportunity to develop valuable life skills in a fun and creative environment. From delicious sweet treats to tasty savoury dishes, children learn how to prepare, cook and present a range of recipes while building confidence in the kitchen. Best of all, they take home their creations to share with family and friends.
Cost: £7.50 per session.
Children can learn to play the guitar with Fernando Aguera, an experienced and inspiring tutor. Lessons help children build strong musical foundations as they develop technique, rhythm and confidence, progressing from simple melodies to performing a wide range of musical pieces.
Fernando.Aguera@oxfordshire.gov.uk
Piano lessons with Mr Hammond provide children with the opportunity to develop lifelong musical skills. As they learn to read music, improve their technique and build confidence at the keyboard, children progress from simple tunes to more challenging pieces, enjoying the satisfaction of seeing their musical abilities grow.
Our exciting Football Club, led by our new coaching provider, offers children the opportunity to develop their football skills in a fun, supportive and energetic environment. Whether they are taking their first kick or refining their game, every session focuses on teamwork, sportsmanship, confidence and enjoyment.
Cost: £7.50 per session.
Choir Club is open to all children and is a wonderful opportunity to develop confidence, singing skills and a love of music. This year, our main focus will be preparing for our exciting Young Voices concert, where pupils will perform alongside thousands of children from across the country.
There is a small charge for the club, with all proceeds going directly towards funding elements of the Young Voices trip and supporting other musical opportunities and events throughout the year. We can't wait to sing together and create some unforgettable memories!
Cost: £7.50 per session.
If your child is interested in learning an instrument through the Oxfordshire County Music Service, whose teachers also visit our school each week, please visit the Learning an Instrument section of the Oxfordshire County Council website to complete an application. A link to the relevant page can be found here.
Please note that once your child has enrolled with the Oxfordshire County Music Service, their place will automatically continue into the following term unless you notify the service that they wish to stop. This is important to avoid any further charges and to ensure your child is removed from the register.
As part of our commitment to ensuring all children have access to enriching opportunities, the cost of Oxfordshire County Music Service lessons for eligible Pupil Premium children is fully funded by the school.

Governors
The Governing Body’s overarching purpose is to:
work with the Head teacher and staff to ensure the school provides the best education possible for all its pupils
have a positive impact on learning & teaching and of raising standards & achievement
promote community cohesion.
Governors are not expected to make day-to-day decisions about how the school is run, that’s the responsibility of the Head teacher. Governors have three key roles in discharging their duties. These are:
setting the school’s vision and strategic aims through agreeing plans and policies and making creative use of available resources
monitoring and evaluating performance and acting as a critical friend to the Head teacher, to support and challenge them in managing the school
ensuring that the school is accountable to the learners and parents it serves, to its local community and to the staff it employs.
This means that Governors are involved in deciding how the budget should be spent, making sure the school buildings are welcoming and safe, setting and monitoring the school’s aims and policies and agreeing the curriculum.
The Governing Body work as a team for the benefit of the school. They respect each other’s points of view but always act as a corporate body and accept the decisions reached by the majority.
A large portion of Governors work is undertaken through various committees by delegation from the Governing Body.
A good and effective working relationship with the Head teacher and other staff at the school is paramount and all Governors are committed to maintaining this as an essential part of their success.
The Governing Body has representatives from various sections of the school and community. The groups from which Governors are drawn are:
people from the community
appointees of the Local Authority
This mix helps Governing Bodies reflect the communities they serve. What’s really important is that they work as part of a team, giving commitment to the school and is an opportunity to make a difference and to put something back into the community.
The Governing Body is always looking for individuals that have energy, enthusiasm, time and a real desire to help provide children with the best possible education. What’s really important is that the School has a good mix of people from their local community and from all walks of life, who can bring different viewpoints, experience, skills and fresh ideas.
You’ll need to be able to give some time to attend meetings and read the paperwork. The school has a Full Governing Body meeting once a term and you would also join a committee, which usually meets once per half term.
Being a school Governor is an opportunity to put something back into your community and to make a difference. It is widely recognised that good governance has a positive impact on standards of attainment, quality of leaning & teaching and pupil behaviour.
School governors can really make a difference in improving standards throughout the school.
If you would like more information please contact the school.

PE and Sport Premium
What is the PE and Sport Premium?
The Primary PE and Sport Premium is a government initiative designed to increase and improve physical education and sporting opportunities for all children. Funding is provided jointly by the Department for Education, the Department for Health and Social Care, and the Department for Culture, Media and Sport.
This funding is allocated directly to primary schools and is ring-fenced, meaning it must be used specifically to develop PE, sport, and physical activity provision within school.
Our Commitment at Peppard
At Peppard Church of England Primary School, we recognise the vital role that physical education and sport play in the lives of children. Through PE, pupils develop not only their physical skills and fitness but also key personal qualities such as teamwork, perseverance, respect, and resilience — all of which are closely linked to our school values of Kindness, Respect, and Perseverance.
We believe that participation in high-quality PE and sport promotes healthy lifestyles, builds self-esteem and confidence, and supports children’s emotional and mental wellbeing. Our goal is for every child to experience the joy and benefits of physical activity and to build habits that last a lifetime.
We are committed to ensuring that all pupils receive at least one hour each week of well-planned, high-quality PE, delivered by confident and well-trained staff.
For the academic year 2024–25, Peppard Church of England Primary School will receive £16,000 in PE and Sport Premium funding.
Our Plans for 2024–25
We will use this funding to:
Monitoring the Impact of Our Spending
We are committed to evaluating the impact of our PE and Sport Premium funding to ensure it makes a meaningful difference for all pupils.
We will monitor progress through:
Our PE Subject Leader will track participation and engagement to ensure all children are accessing a variety of physical activities. They will also support staff with professional development and team-teaching opportunities to build confidence and skill in delivering PE.
Governors will meet regularly with the PE Subject Leader to review spending and ensure funding continues to promote physical activity, wellbeing, and sport across the school.

Our Curriculum
Encouraging Every Child to Flourish
At Peppard Church of England Primary School, our curriculum is rooted in our Christian vision:
"Encourage one another and build each other up."1 Thessalonians 5:11
This vision shapes every aspect of school life and is lived through our values of Kindness, Respect and Perseverance. We believe every child is unique, valued by God and capable of achieving great things.
Our curriculum is ambitious, carefully sequenced and designed to ensure every child develops the knowledge, skills and character they need to flourish both now and in the future. Alongside high academic standards, we nurture curiosity, resilience, confidence and compassion so that every child leaves Peppard ready for the next stage of their education and prepared to make a positive contribution to the world around them.
Our Curriculum Intent
Our curriculum has been carefully designed to ensure that children learn more, remember more and achieve more. Knowledge and skills are progressively built throughout each year so that learning develops securely over time.
Through our curriculum we aim to:
provide a broad, balanced and ambitious education for every child;
inspire curiosity and a lifelong love of learning;
develop confident readers, writers, mathematicians and communicators;
encourage children to think deeply, ask questions and solve problems;
nurture confidence, resilience and independence;
promote spiritual, moral, social and cultural development through our Christian foundation;
prepare children to become responsible citizens who demonstrate Kindness, Respect and Perseverance; and
ensure every child, regardless of their starting point, reaches their full potential.
Bringing Learning to Life
Learning at Peppard extends well beyond the classroom. As a small rural Church of England primary school, we make full use of our unique setting and strong community partnerships to enrich learning.
Our curriculum is enhanced through:
Forest School and outdoor learning on Peppard Common;
educational visits and residential experiences;
music, art, sport and performance opportunities;
leadership responsibilities and pupil voice;
visitors, workshops and community projects;
close links with All Saints Church; and
a wide range of clubs and enrichment opportunities.
These experiences deepen children's understanding, broaden their horizons and help them make meaningful connections across the curriculum whilst developing confidence, teamwork and leadership.
High-Quality Teaching
High-quality teaching sits at the heart of our curriculum.
Lessons are carefully planned using evidence-informed approaches that help children build secure understanding and retain learning over time. Teachers use effective questioning, modelling, retrieval practice and adaptive teaching to ensure every child is supported, challenged and able to succeed.
Reading is at the heart of our curriculum. Children first learn to read and then read to learn, enabling them to access the full curriculum, develop rich vocabulary and foster a lifelong love of books.
Every Child Included
We believe every child deserves to succeed.
Our curriculum is ambitious for all learners. Through adaptive teaching, appropriate support and high expectations, we ensure that every child including those with SEND, disadvantaged pupils and higher-attaining learners can access the full curriculum and achieve success from their individual starting points.
Enrichment and Personal Development
We believe education is about much more than academic achievement.
Our Enrichment Strategy ensures every child experiences a rich range of opportunities that develop confidence, character and cultural understanding. Whether representing the school in sport, performing in productions, taking part in community projects, leading worship, exploring nature or attending residential visits, children develop the knowledge, skills and values needed to flourish in modern Britain.
The Difference Our Curriculum Makes
Our curriculum prepares children not only for secondary school but for life.
Children leave Peppard as confident, curious and compassionate learners who demonstrate Kindness, Respect and Perseverance every day. They possess secure academic knowledge, think critically, communicate effectively and approach challenges with resilience and determination.
Above all, they leave with the confidence, character and values to flourish in whatever path they choose.

Pupil Premium
The Pupil Premium is a government initiative that provides additional funding to schools to support pupils who may face barriers to learning and to help them achieve their full potential. At Peppard Church of England Primary School, we recognise that pupils’ personal and family circumstances can affect their progress and attainment.
The funding is allocated based on the number of pupils eligible for free school meals, those who have been eligible at any point in the last six years, and pupils who are looked after or previously looked after by a local authority. The funding is intended to support schools in narrowing any gaps in outcomes between these pupils and their peers.
At Peppard Church of England Primary School, we are aware that some pupils experience challenges such as low confidence, attendance or punctuality difficulties, behavioural needs, or complex family circumstances. We are committed to supporting all pupils who face such challenges, whether or not they are eligible for pupil premium funding, in line with our Christian values of inclusion, compassion and care for one another.
The Governing Board monitors the school’s use of pupil premium funding to ensure it is used effectively and has a positive impact on outcomes for eligible pupils. Information about how the funding is allocated and the impact it has is published on the school website in line with Department for Education requirements.

School Closure Information
Dear Parents and Carers,
As we approach the time of year when adverse weather may occur, we would like to remind you of the process for checking if the school is closed.
If it becomes necessary to close the school, a message will be posted on the school website as early as possible, and no later than 8:00 am on the day of the closure. We will also update the County Council’s School Closure website, display a notice on the school gates and make announcements through our social media accounts.
Please assume that any closure will initially be for one day only. If conditions continue to be unsafe, you should check the websites each morning for updates.
If you have any questions about this process, please contact the school office before any potential bad weather.
